user_questions.question: 'Make reviews better' doesn't say what should change. The org has Review__c (Storefront, Customer, Rating, Comments, Status, Order Date). What outcome do you want: (a) data quality (required rating/comments, valid ranges), (b) automation (e.g., alert storefront owner on low ratings, average rating roll-up), (c) a moderation workflow on Status, or (d) something else? Recommendation: tell me the problem you see today.
user_questions.simulated_answer: Merchants should be able to respond publicly to reviews - add Merchant Response text + Response Date on Review, and notify the reviewer.

skill_friction: The vague-requirement rule says to ask one clarifying question before calling AskCoworker, but it does not say whether read-only org queries may be run first to ground the options. I ran sobject list/describe so the question could name Review__c; the rule could say this explicitly.

The requirement text sent to AskCoworker stays verbatim ('make reviews better') while the real scope comes from the clarification. The template covers this by putting the clarification under 'Established so far', but for vague cases it leaves the Requirement line nearly meaningless.

AskCoworker repeatedly tagged facts I had sent as '[Verified: prior session]'. The response-handling table treats echoed facts as established, but the label looks like prior-session memory. The skill could say that such labels on echoed facts need no action.

Spec-format requires placement for UI fields but gives no guidance for when both a Dynamic Forms FlexiPage and a layout exist. I updated both (FlexiPage activation could not be verified); minimal design (Rule 4) arguably says update only the FlexiPage.
Section 7 guidance recommends FlowTest metadata for flow-only changes but does not say whether a FlowTest should be an inventory row. I left it as recommended verification.
